_format: Hand-written explanations shown under a leaderboard row. Key = library entry id (e.g. "curl_cffi|chrome146", see libraries.json "id") or a bare library name (e.g. "curl_cffi") to apply to all its profiles; an id key wins. Value = a string or a list of strings. Keys starting with _ are ignored. Rebuild with: python leaderboard/build.py --annotate-only && site/sync.sh
tls-client|chrome_152_psk: Best pick today: in v1.16.0 this profile matched current Chrome's default fingerprint exactly, including resumed connections.
tls-client|chrome_152: Fresh handshakes match Chrome exactly, but switch to Chrome_152_PSK if you need session resumption to look like Chrome too.
tls-client|chrome_150: Matches Chrome only with trust anchors turned off (the no_ca34 variant), so prefer Chrome_152_PSK in the same release.
curl_cffi|chrome150: Newest curl_cffi profile we tested (0.16.3); it matches Chrome only with trust anchors turned off, so it lacks the ca34 extension default Chrome now sends.
curl_cffi|chrome146: Upgrade to the chrome150 profile in the same curl_cffi 0.16.3 release, which only lacks trust anchors.
curl_cffi|chrome136: Upgrade to the chrome150 profile in the same curl_cffi 0.16.3 release, which only lacks trust anchors.
rnet|chrome137: Chrome145 is the newer rnet profile we tested, but it has the same two gaps.
noble-tls: Wraps Go tls-client, whose own Chrome_152_PSK profile matched current Chrome exactly.
tls-client (Python): Wraps Go tls-client; using Go tls-client v1.16.0 with Chrome_152_PSK directly matched current Chrome exactly.
uTLS: Tested with Go's golang.org/x/net/http2 because uTLS only does TLS, so the HTTP/2 settings mismatch reflects that pairing rather than uTLS alone.
